verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI ships its own natural-language interfaces. The `clai` CLI lets users chat from the command line or in a browser, `Agent.to_cli_sync()` turns any agent into a chat CLI, and the docs describe a complete terminal coding agent with file access, an allowlisted shell and planning. However, the evidence never shows the framework itself being configured or operated through natural-language commands; the core product is still driven by Python code. Missing for 10: documented natural-language control of the framework's own setup and operations (building and configuring agents, evals, deployment), and independent hands-on corroboration of the NL interfaces.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Pydantic AI comes with a CLI, clai (pronounced “clay”). You can use it to chat with various LLMs and quickly get answers, right from the command line
spin up a uvicorn server to chat with your Pydantic AI agents from your browser.
you can directly launch CLI mode from an Agent instance using Agent.to_cli_sync().
A complete coding agent in your terminal: workspace-rooted file access, allowlisted shell, repo orientation, planning, and context management that survives long sessions.
